extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in personalized news recommendation / recommender systems
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and criteria for modeling news items and user profiles in personalized news recommender systems, covering feature choices (property, context, content, graph, multimodal) and modeling techniques (feature-based and deep learning).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use news property features (categories, locations, publishers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Property features such as categories, locations and publishers usually reflect intrinsic properties of news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category is the most widely used property feature; when editorial category labels are unavailable, cluster news into categories (e.g., hierarchical clustering based on LDA as in SCENE). Incorporate categories/clusters to make recommenders aware of news topics and target user interest. Use geographic information to filter/provide location-related news. Include publisher metadata because different publishers differ in content and topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use dynamic context features (popularity, recency, timestamp)
rubrics_metrics.description: Context features of news are dynamic. Popularity and recency reflect attractiveness and freshness of news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model news importance/recency (e.g., MONERS) and include finer-grained timestamps (weekday, hour, season, month, time-of-day) for impression-level modeling (e.g., Ilievski et al.). Popularity and recency often strongly influence click prediction and can surpass personalized signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploit near-real-time signals such as CTR and popularity
rubrics_metrics.description: Click-through rate (CTR) and near-real-time popularity are used to enrich news representations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate near-real-time CTR or predicted CTR into news features or gating mechanisms (e.g., PP-Rec) to synthesize CTR, recency and popularity. Note practical limitations: near-real-time CTR may be unavailable in some real-world systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include environmental/contextual features (weather, location, time)
rubrics_metrics.description: Environmental/contextual factors like weather, user/news location and time can be useful for contextualized recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use weather features and location-aware filtering to provide locally relevant news (e.g., Tavakolifard et al.). Use timestamps of display for fine-grained behavior modeling (season, hour). Be mindful of privacy and availability constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model fact/opinion bias and sentiment
rubrics_metrics.description: Use fact/opinion bias and sentiment orientation as features to enrich news representations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute sentiment scores (e.g., VADER in SentiRec) to learn sentiment-aware representations; include bias indicators to avoid recommending overly biased content and to protect user experience/platform reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine ID-based and content-based representations (hybrid modeling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hybrid methods consider both news IDs and additional features to represent news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concatenate or jointly use news IDs with features (bag-of-words, topics, click frequency, category weights) to mitigate cold-start to some extent (examples: NewsWeeder, Claypool). Be cautious: news IDs have limited coverage due to short news lifecycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use bag-of-words / TF‑IDF / topic models for feature-based text modeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Handcrafted textual features such as BOW/TF‑IDF and topic models like LDA are widely used to represent news texts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topic models capture topic distributions useful for inferring user interests; entities/keywords derived from text can summarize content and link to knowledge graphs. Limitation: handcrafted features require domain knowledge and may miss contextual/sequence information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage neural embedding approaches (autoencoders, doc2vec, word2vec)
rubrics_metrics.description: Embedding-based neural methods learn dense representations of news texts (e.g., EBNR uses denoising autoencoders; RA‑DSSM uses doc2vec; 3‑D‑CNN uses word2vec).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use neural encoders to replace handcrafted features and capture semantic similarity. Early neural models can still be shallow and miss deep contextual semantics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt deep text models (CNNs, self-attention/Transformers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advanced neural NLP architectures (CNN, multi-head self-attention, Transformers) are effective for news text modeling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use CNNs for local context and efficiency; use attention mechanisms to select informative words; use Transformer-like architectures (e.g., NRMS) to capture richer contexts. Combine with attention for aggregating multi-part inputs (title, body).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use pretrained language models (PLMs) to improve text understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Large pretrained language models (e.g., BERT) can significantly improve news text understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate PLMs (PLM‑NR, UNBERT, etc.) for richer semantic representations; consider multilingual vs English PLMs depending on corpus. Note computational/latency costs and potential need for fine-tuning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate entities and keywords to bring knowledge/commonsense
rubrics_metrics.description: Use entities or keywords extracted from news texts to add complementary knowledge and commonsense information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Represent entities as text embeddings, concatenate entity and text representations, and use attention to weight their informativeness (e.g., Gao et al., DAN, DNA). Be aware of many emergent entities that may not be covered by KBs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate knowledge graph embeddings
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowledge graph embeddings (TransE, TransD, etc.) can represent entity relations and enrich news representations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct news-relevant knowledge graphs or subgraphs and combine KG embeddings with text embeddings (e.g., DKN, TEKGR, KRED). Use GNNs/graph attention to capture higher-order relations. Limitations: KG embeddings often encode low-level interactions and KB coverage gaps for new entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensemble multi-view inputs (titles, bodies, categories, subcategories, tags)
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat different news information types as separate views and aggregate their embeddings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process title, body, category, subcategory, tags, keywords, entities via specialized encoders and fuse with view-level attention or fully connected layers (e.g., NAML, TANR, CHAMELEON) to form unified news representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use auxiliary prediction tasks (topic/metadata prediction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Auxiliary tasks such as predicting news topics or metadata help encode metadata-aware representations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train auxiliary predictors (e.g., topic prediction in TANR, metadata prediction in CHAMELEON) jointly to inject topic/category signals into representations and improve downstream recommendation performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model visual and multimodal information
rubrics_metrics.description: Visual content of news (images, layout, spatial positions) provides additional cues for recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use visiolinguistic models (e.g., ViLBERT) or models capturing image regions, arrangement, and spatial positions (IMRec, MM‑Rec). Note that many personalized systems still omit visual features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model presentation bias and positional features
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentation features (position, size, display bias) affect click behavior and can be modeled to learn bias-aware representations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn bias embeddings or bias-aware components (e.g., DebiasRec learns news bias from size/position and a bias model) and incorporate into content modeling or use for debiasing user signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use graph-based news representations (user-news, heterogeneous graphs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Graph methods learn news representations from user-news interaction graphs or heterogeneous graphs combining topics/users/news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply GNNs/GAT/GCN on user-news or user-news-topic graphs to exploit high-order collaborative signals (e.g., IGNN, MVL, GNewsRec). Be cautious: static graphs are hard to adapt for newly generated news with few connections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be mindful of feature availability and privacy constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Some features (category labels, CTR, demographics, location) may be unavailable or privacy-sensitive in real deployments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design models that can operate without privileged signals; consider privacy-preserving approaches and gracefully degrade when features are missing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid over-reliance on handcrafted features (tradeoffs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Handcrafted feature-based methods require domain knowledge and may not optimally capture contextual/ordered language information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer learned representations (deep models/PLMs) for richer semantics, but combined approaches (handcrafted + learned) can still be useful when labeled data or compute is limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate clicked-news features for user representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Represent users by aggregating features or learned representations of their clicked news (CF‑IDF, SF‑IDF, averaged LDA features, or learned embeddings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use simple averaging or weighted aggregation; employ attention mechanisms to weight more informative clicks (news-level attention, candidate-aware attention). Consider access patterns and cross-platform behaviors as additional signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate user demographics and location
rubrics_metrics.description: Demographics (age, gender, occupation, socio‑economic grade) and user location help distinguish preferences across groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate demographic features when available (e.g., Yeung et al., Chu et al.) but be aware of privacy sensitivity and potential inaccuracies in self-reported data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use richer user behavior signals beyond clicks (dwell time, read/reject/scroll)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clicks alone may not fully indicate user interest; other behaviors like dwell time, careful reads, rejections and scroll events provide deeper signals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weight clicked news by dwell time (Yi et al.), and treat read/rejected/scrolled differently (Gershman et al.) to build more accurate user models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploit graph-based user representations (hypergraphs, browsing graphs, context trees)
rubrics_metrics.description: Represent users via subgraphs of hypergraphs or browsing graphs to capture high-order interactions and browsing context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build hypergraph/graph structures from sequences, topics, entities (e.g., Li et al., Trevisiol et al., Joseph et al.) and apply graph algorithms to derive user embeddings. Useful for capturing habits and cross-item relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model long-term and short-term user interests separately
rubrics_metrics.description: User interests evolve; modeling both long-term and short-term interests yields better personalization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Represent long-term interest via aggregated topic/tag frequency or weighted history; short-term interest via most recent clicks or session-based representations (e.g., LOGO, NewsDude). Combine via weighted summation or hybrid models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use attention and candidate-aware aggregation for user modeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Attention mechanisms select important clicks and candidate-aware attention weights historical clicks by relevance to candidate news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply news-level attention (NAML, KRED) or candidate-aware attention (DKN, TEKGR) to form user embeddings that emphasize behavior most relevant to current candidates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model sequential dependencies with RNNs but consider limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: RNNs (GRU, LSTM, Bi‑LSTM) model sequential dependencies in click histories and user interest dynamics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use RNNs for sequential dynamics (e.g., EBNR, RA‑DSSM, DAN) but note they may be weak in capturing global interest diversity and news recommendation may not fit conventional sequential-recommendation assumptions; consider combining with attention or global models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply hierarchical and disentangled interest modeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Model user interest at multiple granularity levels (subtopic → topic → overall) and disentangle preferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use hierarchical models (HieRec) to form subtopic-level and topic-level interest representations before aggregating. Use disentanglement regularization (GNUD) for preference disentanglement on graphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debias user modeling to account for presentation and exposure biases
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentation bias (position, size) and exposure biases distort click signals; incorporate bias-aware components to learn debiased user representations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate bias models (DebiasRec) or bias-aware aggregation to adjust attention/weights for observed clicks; necessary for more truthful interest inference.
